ConocoPhillips dropped 2.4% today as oil prices fell—U.S. crude slipped to $89.53 per barrel, down from recent highs—and broader energy sector momentum shifted sharply. The collapse of climate negotiations at COP31, which failed to restrict fossil fuels as many had feared, initially looked positive for oil stocks, but that boost was overshadowed by a larger trend: Wall Street analysts and market commentary are now signaling that the exceptional run in refinery and energy stocks is unwinding, pulling investors out of the sector overall.

The pullback also reflects how fragile the near-term setup is. While geopolitical tensions in the Middle East (Houthi attacks on Saudi refineries) typically support oil prices, they haven't been enough to hold them steady here—suggesting demand concerns or profit-taking may be outweighing supply-risk premiums. The stock is down roughly 5% over the past week despite relatively stable oil prices, pointing to sector rotation away from energy rather than an oil-price story alone.
